title: Autonomic latency-fence router with capacity shepherd and soft geo-pinning
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Design and implement an autonomic multi-region request router that enforces latency SLO fences while steering to capacity-aware pools and honoring soft geo-pinning credits. Objective: reduce p99 regional latency violations during partial outages by routing traffic to alternative regions or degraded model variants without violating customer-configured locality preferences more than a configurable budget.
acceptance_criteria: Router applies latency fence per customer route: if observed p95 latency > configured fence for 30s, trigger soft-evacuation flow
Soft geo-pin credits respected: traffic will remain in pinned region until credit budget exhausted, then route out with annotation for audit
Capacity-aware steering prevents overload: destination node groups have admission/checkpointing to reject requests early when token capacity exhausted
Circuit breaker trips and forces fast-fail with clear HTTP 503 & error metadata when all alternative pools exceed thresholds
End-to-end canary rollout shows lower p99 violations vs baseline under synthetic capacity degradation (>= 15% improvement)
design_decisions: Latency fences are defined as per-route SLO knobs (p95/p99 targets) and implemented as moving-window quantile checks in the steering service
Soft pin model: each pinned customer receives a daily credit bucket (fractional requests or time-based) which decays when cross-region routing occurs; credits replenish on a configurable cadence
Capacity tokens: each destination pool exposes an RPC for current token availability; router performs best-effort token reservation before dispatch to avoid thundering herd

Circuit breaker tiers: (1) pool-level admission (rejects with retry-after), (2) route-level shedder (priority-queue drop for low-priority requests), (3) global fast-fail fallback to composed error with recovery hints
Fallback model variants: when full-precision models are constrained, automatically route to quantized/compact variant with explicit annotation to downstream telemetry
Telemetry and observability: every decision emits structured attributes (decision.reason, source_region, dest_region, capacity_tokens, credit_before/after) to tracing and metrics

comments: 2026-03-10 Ava Thompson: Created ticket after postmortem of INC-2026-03-07 where eu-west region experienced elevated tail latency and a spike in cross-region failover errors. Goal: reduce blast radius and honor customer locality preferences.

2026-03-11 Rohit Malhotra: Spike finished for moving-window quantile check. Prototype shows 2s evaluation window with 60% overlap yields stable fence detection. PR #4123 opened for steering changes (WIP).
2026-03-12 Jane Park (SRE): Suggested adding a fast-path circuit-breaker that replies with 503 + X-RW-Advice header to allow SDKs to implement local retries. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-13 Rohit Malhotra: Implemented token reservation RPC in pool manager; integrated basic backpressure response. Benchmarks on staging: reservation adds 0.6ms median to dispatch but reduces concurrent overload events.

2026-03-14 Design review notes: PM (Liam Ortiz) approved soft-pin credit model but asked to cap cross-region routed fraction per customer to 10% unless explicitly overridden. Added release gating and opt-in flag for enterprise tenants.
notes: Rollout will be feature-flagged. Start canary in us-east-1 with 1% of traffic, expand to eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 after 48h of stable metrics. Emergency rollback = toggle feature flag off + clear token reservations. Ensure SLO alerting augmentation on routing-decision churn metric.
